paragraphs: R. Meyasha, grandson of R. Yehoshua ben Levi, Jerusalem Talmud, Berakhot 2, mishnah 3; Beitzah 1, halakhah 6; Babylonian Berakhot 24b. There 23a, 'son of R. Yehoshua ben Levi' is a scribal error, uncorrected in שס״ח [provisionally the new Shas]. He was a Levite, Ḥullin 106b. In Yehoshua ben Levi's name, HaMaddir 75a. Jerusalem Talmud, end of Shemonah Sheratzim and Avodah Zarah 2, halakhah 2: Yehoshua ben Levi's grandson had a throat affliction (belaʿ); a certain man whispered an incantation for him, etc., and he recovered. On leaving, he asked what he had whispered. He answered, 'Such-and-such words.' He said, 'It would have been better had he died'; it was like an error issuing from a ruler. He died holding a deposit. Its owner supplied an identifying sign; R. Ammi said, 'I know he was not wealthy,' Ketubbot 85b. Meyasha, Yehoshua ben Levi's grandson, lay sunk in illness for three days and said, 'Many people I saw honored here are disgraced there.' When R. Yoḥanan and Resh Lakish heard, they visited him, Midrash Ruth, 'Where you die, I shall die.' See Yosef son of Yehoshua ben Levi for this incident. Rabbah, end of Aḥarei Mot, has 'R. Menashya, grandson of Yehoshua ben Levi': a scribal error.
